Subject: CI artifacts: OPA rules + pipeline enforcement examples (draft)

Hi all — attaching the first bundle for review. Highlights below and attachments referenced.

Quick summary:
- Enforcement point: OPA gate runs in the CI runner container immediately after checkout and before build step. If policy evaluation returns "deny" the job exits with code 1; pipeline status = failed; PR status is set to "policy-failed" via our GitHub checks integration.
- Failure handling: failed jobs create an incident ticket in PagerDuty (policy-fail routing) and send a Slack summary to #sec-opa for triage. Emergency approval is supported via a short-lived signed approval link that triggers an internal workflow (documented in pipeline-step-examples.md).
- OPA bundle: included as ci-opa-policies-20261012.tar.gz (sample policies only; no customer data). The bundle contains rule examples for branch protection, image vulnerability thresholds, and denylists for unapproved cloud credentials.

Attachments in this message:
- ci-opa-policies-20261012.tar.gz (OPA policy bundle, sample rules only)
- pipeline-step-examples.md (markdown with exact YAML snippets we use in GitHub Actions and GitLab CI)
- ci-enforcement-screenshots-20261012.png (check-run examples)

Example snippet (from pipeline-step-examples.md):
---
name: policy-check
uses: actions/checkout@v3
run: |
  docker run --rm -v $GITHUB_WORKSPACE:/workspace redwood/opa-check:stable 
    /workspace/ci-opa-policies --input /workspace/pr-meta.json || exit 1
---

Notes: the docker image references a signed digest; the image pull is restricted to our registry and scanned nightly.

Let me know if you want the raw pipeline run IDs (I can redact job IDs but include timestamps).

—Marissa
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Folks —

I've attached the secret custody matrix and included a short explanation below for the assessor. Key points to call out in the README:

- Secrets store: We use Vault (HashiCorp) as the authoritative custody for build-time secrets; keys to Vault are provisioned by our platform team using ephemeral AppRole tokens with TTL = 15m for CI jobs.
- Ephemeral credentials: For cloud API access during builds we create ephemeral STS tokens (max 1h), bound to task-specific IAM roles. These are never persisted in artifacts.
- Rotation & owners: Secrets rotation is on a 90-day schedule for long-lived tokens (service accounts). Build-only credentials use the ephemeral approach, no rotation required. A columned matrix is attached (secret-custody-matrix-20261012.xlsx) mapping secret type -> owner -> rotation -> audit-source.
- Audit logs: Vault audit device is enabled and writes to our log cluster; sample audit snippets (timestamps, event type, redacted accessor IDs) are in the Drive link. We will provide redacted log lines; full accessor IDs are sensitive and will be redacted per our disclosure policy.

Quoting Marissa for context:
> Enforcement point: OPA gate runs in the CI runner container immediately after checkout and before build step. If policy evaluation returns "deny" the job exits with code 1; pipeline status = failed...

I'll also include the OPA policy evaluation telemetry (metrics and example alert rules) as a short appendix.

-Neha
Principal Cloud Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
